source.pages: 3-4 (printed): Table 1 pp. 3-4 (PDF pages 7-8); equipment Table 2 p. 4; Figure 1 p. 2
source.cite: Fluke 374 / 375 / 376 / 376-II Calibration Manual, Table 1 Performance Tests, printed pp. 3-4; limits unchanged, rows flagged against the published accuracy (UNVERIFIED source, see Source)
source.report_note: Limits are those of the manufacturer's Table 1 (Fluke 374 / 375 / 376 / 376-II Calibration Manual, printed pp. 3-4), unchanged. The jaw and iFlex current points are driven through a 50-turn coil (calibrator current x 50 = the reading shown); the iFlex simulated points apply a voltage to the iFlex input. Their Uncertainty is the calibrator's uncertainty at the actual output (current: point / 50, unscaled and without the coil; simulation: AC volts as applied), an owner-chosen convention; TAR / TUR compare it with the meter-reading tolerance for the coil points and are blank for the iFlex simulated points.
source.note: Table 1 (38 rows: AC volts 4, DC volts 8 (4 of them millivolts), ohms 7, capacitance 3, AC amps 4, DC amps 3, iFlex simulated 5, iFlex with coil 4; printed pp. 3-4 of the 374 / 375 / 376 / 376-II Calibration Manual). The table has no step numbers: steps are numbered in table order (1-1 .. 1-38). One family spec: the X columns decide the models (374: 28 points, 375: 34, 376 and 376-II: 38). Table 2 (printed p. 4) names a calibrator with 4.5 digit resolution (Fluke 55XXA recommended), the 55XXA/COIL (50 turns), the test probe for iFlex and a test lead; the procedure drives a Fluke 5522A or 5560A (or you set the calibrator by hand). The current rows are driven through the 50-turn coil: the calibrator output is 0.2 / 10 / 18 / 6 A and the meter reads 50 x that (limits are meter readings). The iFlex rows are simulated with a voltage (3 to 750 mV) or driven through the coil with the iFlex loop. The meter has no remote interface: you type the display reading. Limits are as printed (nothing is corrected). Where a printed limit is not the full or half published accuracy (UNVERIFIED source, the fluke.com product page) the point says so. High-voltage points go straight to the test value (the manual prescribes no ramp). The calibration ADJUSTMENT (Table 3, printed pp. 5-8) is not part of this procedure.

COIL_AUX.title: Change the cables: 50-turn coil on the calibrator low-current output
COIL_AUX.summary: Calibrator low-current output (5522A AUX HI / AUX LO; 5560A VI AUX / OUTPUT LO) -> 50-turn coil (55XXA/COIL) -> the meter jaw closed around the coil. No test leads in the meter jacks.
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Test leads
REMOVE the test leads from the VΩ and COM jacks while the current is measured with the jaw or the iFlex (general practice; the Calibration Manual does not say).
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Coil

The wired coil is 50 turns (Table 2, printed p. 4: 55XXA/COIL). Connect its two ends to the calibrator: Fluke 5522A AUX HI and AUX LO; Fluke 5560A VI AUX (HI) and OUTPUT LO. Use plugs rated for the current.
Jaw

Close the detachable jaw around the coil, jaw fully closed, the coil centred in the opening, the coil leads kept away from the meter body. The meter then reads 50 x the calibrator current: 0.2 A reads 10 A. (How the jaw sits on the 55XXA/COIL is not described in the manual: UNVERIFIED.)
LCOMP
Fluke 5522A: for the AC points switch inductive-load compensation (LCOMP) ON at the calibrator front panel when the coil needs it. The program does not set it: UNVERIFIED for this coil.
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
COIL_AUX.caution: This point drives current through a coil. Keep the calibrator in STANDBY whenever you touch the coil or leads. The jaw is marked 1000 A, CAT III 1000 V (Figure 1).

COIL_20A.title: Change the cables: 50-turn coil on the calibrator high-current output
COIL_20A.summary: Calibrator high-current output (5522A 20 A / AUX LO; 5560A 30A / OUTPUT LO) -> 50-turn coil (55XXA/COIL) -> the meter jaw closed around the coil. No test leads in the meter jacks.
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Test leads
REMOVE the test leads from the VΩ and COM jacks while the current is measured with the jaw or the iFlex (general practice; the Calibration Manual does not say).
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Coil
Move the two ends of the 50-turn coil to the calibrator high-current terminals: Fluke 5522A 20 A and AUX LO; Fluke 5560A 30A and OUTPUT LO. The coil, plugs and leads must carry up to 18 A.
Jaw

The detachable jaw stays closed around the coil (centred, jaw fully closed, leads away from the meter body). The meter reads 50 x the calibrator current: 10 A reads 500 A, 18 A reads 900 A, 6 A reads 300 A.
LCOMP
Fluke 5522A: AC points with LCOMP ON when the coil needs it (not set by the program; UNVERIFIED for this coil).
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
COIL_20A.caution: Up to 18 A flows in the coil. The 5500A/COIL data recorded in NOTES.md allows 11 A continuously and 20 A for 2 minutes (then 8 minutes rest): UNVERIFIED for this coil. Keep the calibrator in STANDBY whenever you touch the coil or leads; check that the coil and leads are not warm after a long run.

IFLEX_SIM.title: Change the cables: iFlex simulation (calibrator voltage output to the iFlex input)
IFLEX_SIM.summary: Calibrator NORMAL HI (5522A) / OUTPUT V/Ω HI (5560A) -> iFlex 2 mm jack (far left); calibrator LO -> the black COM jack. Test lead with retractable sheath (6358, PN 1903307) and 2 mm to 4 mm Slim Reach probe (PN 6508922).
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Calibrator
Fluke 5522A: NORMAL HI and NORMAL LO; Fluke 5560A: OUTPUT V/Ω HI and OUTPUT V/Ω LO (the voltage output, as for the volts points).
iFlex input

Calibrator HI to the iFlex 2 mm jack on the far left of the meter, calibrator LO to the black COM jack (Performance Tests, printed p. 3). Use the test probe for iFlex (2 mm to 4 mm Slim Reach probe, PN 6508922) and the test lead with retractable sheath (6358, PN 1903307) from the equipment list. No iFlex loop is connected. Which jack is the "far left" one is UNVERIFIED (Figure 1 shows the jacks too small to name).
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
IFLEX_SIM.caution: The output is only millivolts (3 to 750 mV). Keep the calibrator in STANDBY while you connect the leads.

IFLEX_COIL_AUX.title: Change the cables: iFlex loop on the 50-turn coil, calibrator low-current output
IFLEX_COIL_AUX.summary: Calibrator low-current output (5522A AUX HI / AUX LO; 5560A VI AUX / OUTPUT LO) -> 50-turn coil (55XXA/COIL) -> the iFlex loop around the coil, plugged into the meter. No test leads in the meter jacks.
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Test leads
REMOVE the test leads from the VΩ and COM jacks while the current is measured with the jaw or the iFlex (general practice; the Calibration Manual does not say).
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Coil
Coil on the calibrator low-current output as for the jaw points: Fluke 5522A AUX HI and AUX LO; Fluke 5560A VI AUX (HI) and OUTPUT LO.
iFlex

Remove the jaw from the coil. Plug the iFlex probe into the meter and place its loop around the coil (Table 1, printed p. 4: iFlex Current Probe with 50-turn coil). The meter reads 50 x the calibrator current: 0.2 A reads 10 A. How the loop sits on the 55XXA/COIL (position, closed latch, away from the leads) is not described in the manual: UNVERIFIED.
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
IFLEX_COIL_AUX.caution: This point drives current through a coil. Keep the calibrator in STANDBY whenever you touch the coil, the loop or the leads.
